payload.selection_rationale:
Only one proposal came in (practice), and its own over_engineering_flag is the reason it was selected and not set aside. Before writing this, every claim it makes about existing code was checked against the tree: the Append/SetChildren/AddFlags/CheckParent/Charges bodies in ScanStore.cs, the Kind-byte branches in ScanStore.Rollup.cs, ListRoot/Execute/FolderDone/StoreSkipped/IsDue in Scanner.cs, ShowOutcome in MainWindow.xaml.cs, and Scans.EntryState, RunCancellingAt, CancelledFolderTests, RollupOracle.Feed/Expected/CheckStructure and the MemoryBudget collection in the tests. All of them hold.

It matches what reality has already settled:
- U-201 (CONDITIONAL). It meets the conditions that apply to a Flags-only mark: only Append sets it, only SetChildren clears it, AddFlags refuses it, and code that compares flags for equality must not see it. The Kind-masking condition does not arise, because SubtreeUnfinished is dropped.
- The risk spike's no-go prerequisite (h). Without an early append, a Stop in the root's listing leaves no root to mark. The design meets this by appending the root right after the directory check. That point is earlier than the spike's validated "before the first List call", and also covers calls 3-5, which the spike reported still left no root.
- The go SMB-stall spike. A cut folder returns 995 with LastCallAborted, so FolderDone never calls SetChildren and the mark survives.
- U-204 is IMPOSSIBLE as stated (both markers at once), and U-170/U-172 put live cross-thread reads out of scope. The design builds neither.
- The build check measured bit 0x80 as free in the existing Page.Flags byte column. So criterion 7's "no per-entry storage" holds by construction, and only the stopped-at-peak memory figure remains to measure.
- Q-080 (model) said a 'not finished' state for a cancelled folder would be a separate scanner slice. This is that state, and it does not change how the Unreadable record classifies anything.

Against the simplest-thing test, the proposal is the trimmed form of what U-201 and the spike built: one bit, three one-line guards, a masked read, one new read, and one moved call. It reuses the existing deterministic cancel sweep (lesson #98) and the RollupOracle recount instead of new machinery.

What the composer changed:
- Added two text rules the proposal declined. They guard a silent defect: outside the store, a test of the bit against Flags() is always false.
- Made criterion 6's "no edits" a git-diff check.
- Constrained where the container store is planted in the sweep tree, so the committed-folder oracle holds.
- Filed the WPF app's own commit at this shape as later work instead of claiming it.

components.name: ScanStore not-listed mark
components.responsibility:
Adds `private const byte NotListedBit = 0x80`.
- Append rejects a caller-supplied 0x80 with ArgumentException, checked before CheckParent's side-effect-free checks and before any column or `_count` is written. When kind == Folder it ORs the bit into page.Flags[i] before Volatile.Write publishes the count. AppendRoot goes through Append, so the root is marked too.
- SetChildren clears the bit after writing FirstChild and ChildCount, whatever the count.
- AddFlags rejects 0x80 with ArgumentException, next to its HardlinkDuplicate refusal, and leaves the entry unchanged.
- The public Flags(index) returns the stored byte with 0x80 masked off.
- New public read `bool NotListed(int index)`: the raw bit, true only for a folder that was appended and never had its children registered. Out-of-range indices throw through At, like every other read.
- The class remarks gain one sentence: the mark is exact between appends on the writing thread and once Scan has returned, the same contract as the rollups. Charges, CheckParent, Post and every Rollup read are unchanged.
components.key_interactions: CheckParent tests only the Unreadable bit, so a marked folder still accepts its children while FolderDone appends them before SetChildren (Scanner.cs:375-377). The rollups branch on the Kind byte, never on Flags, so a marked folder still reads as a folder. Charges masks only HardlinkDuplicate. IsDue and the probe rule receive the masked Flags(), which are exactly today's values.

components.name: EntryFlags reserved-bit note
components.responsibility: Adds a comment on EntryFlags: bit 0x80 belongs to the store as the not-listed mark. It is never an EntryFlags member and never returned by ScanStore.Flags; read it through ScanStore.NotListed. The next flag needs a new byte column or Kind's free bits (U-201). No member is added, so Enum.GetValues/GetNames and every equality comparison of flags stay exactly as they are.
components.key_interactions: Satisfies criterion 5 by construction. Scans.EntryState record equality on stopped stores (CancelledFolderTests) keeps passing unedited. Pinned by architecture rule 2.

components.name: Scanner: root appended after the directory check
components.responsibility:
In ListRoot, `_store.AppendRoot(display, attributes)` moves up to directly after the FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY check: before DecideLastAccess, the keep reopen, CountListingOpen and _reader.List.
- The rootEntry out-parameter keeps its meaning (0 when there is a listing to commit, -1 otherwise), so Execute's Cancelled/RootUnreadable branch and FolderDone(rootEntry, ...) are unchanged.
- The root's child block still starts at Count == 1, so TopLevelTracker.Seed and progress are unchanged.
- The class remarks change from 'it stays as the scan left every folder it never reached' to say that such a folder, and a folder Cancel cut part-way, reads ScanStore.NotListed.
- No other write changes: FolderDone and StoreSkipped stay the only SetChildren callers.
components.key_interactions: A Stop in the root's open (call 1) or attribute query (call 2), a token cancelled before the scan, a Refused root and a root that is a file all still leave Count 0. RootTests.ARegularFileIsNotARoot, CancellationTests' call-1 and already-cancelled tests, and ContainerLayerStoreTests' refusals all stop at or before that point. A RootUnreadable root whose listing failed with nothing kept now holds one entry, the root reading NotListed. The App returns early on RootUnreadable (MainWindow.xaml.cs:534), so nothing it draws changes.

components.name: NotListedTests
components.responsibility:
A new file with no Trait and no Skip (CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped).

(1) CancelAtAnyCallMarksExactlyTheFoldersNotCommitted(bool during). A sweep of every scan-thread guarded call over a real temp tree:
- 'a-empty' (empty, listed first), 'big' (2,000 names of 100 characters, so it spans several buffers), nested queued folders, an h1/h2 hardlink pair, a folder denied list access with TempTree.Deny, 'm', whose only subfolder is the container layer store planted through ScanOptions.ContainerLayerStorePath, and 'z'.
- The oracle comes from the uncancelled baseline's AfterFolder (progress.CurrentFolder, guard.Calls), as in CancelledFolderTests: a folder is committed if and only if its last call is before k. The store folder counts as committed exactly when 'm' is, because StoreSkipped makes no guarded call and runs at the next pop. AfterFolder does not fire for it.
- At each k it asserts NotListed(e) == (folder && !committed). NotListed implies ChildCount 0, FirstChild -1, Rolled (0,0,0), no Unreadable and no NotScanned. No file or link reads NotListed.

(2) AnEmptyFolderListedBeforeTheStopReadsListed. The build check's probe tree (a-empty, b\c\f.bin, z\g.bin), stopped through AfterFolder after 2 and after 3 folders, plus a completed scan.

(3) AStopInTheRootsListingLeavesTheRootNotListed. Every call of a 2,000-entry root's open, queries and listing, before and during. For k ≤ 2: Count 0. For every later root call: Count 1, NotListed(0), ChildCount(0) 0, status Cancelled, RootError 0.

(4) AStopDuringSizingLeavesEveryFolderListed. The ScanOptions.Probe seam cancels on its first probe; status Cancelled and no entry NotListed.

(5) Store Theories:
- ACallerCannotSetTheMark: Append with 0x80 combined with each named flag, for folder, file and link, throws and leaves Count unchanged. AddFlags with 0x80, on a marked and on a listed folder, throws and leaves the bit as it was.
- AMarkedFolderTakesItsChildrenAndSetChildrenClearsIt: SetChildren with 0 and with n children.
- EveryOtherFlagWriteLeavesTheMarkAlone: AddFlags of every named flag, CorrectSizes, and file and link appends.

(6) AStoppedStoreRecountsWithNoDifference. At several stop points: RollupOracle.Expected and AssertMatches over a Fed stream rebuilt from the stopped store's raw Parent/Kind/Size/OnDisk/FileId columns, plus CheckStructure, plus ChildrenLargestFirst against an independent sort.

(7) AStoppedStoreClassifiesAsItsMaskedTwin. A twin replayed through RollupOracle.Feed (Flags without Unreadable, because CheckParent refuses appends under Unreadable), then SetChildren on every childless folder, then AddFlags(Unreadable). It must equal the stopped store on Flags, Kind, ChargedSize/ChargedOnDisk, Rolled.Of, FirstChild/ChildCount and ChildrenLargestFirst, and Enum.GetValues<EntryFlags>() has no member carrying 0x80.

(8) ACompletedScanLeavesNothingNotListed. Covers the sweep tree and a tree with a junction and a path over 260 characters.
components.key_interactions:
Reuses:
- Scans.RunCancellingAt, WithGuard, AssertChargedBytesAreTheTotals, Snapshot
- TraversalTests.AssertChildrenAreContiguous
- RollupOracle.Feed, Expected, AssertMatches, CheckStructure
- TempTree: Folder, File, Hardlink, Deny, Junction
- ScanOptions: AfterFolder, ContainerLayerStorePath, Probe

The container-store guard in ContainerLayerStore.Resolve is created with announce: false, so the Created hook never arms it and the call numbering is the scan thread's alone. Before sizing the work, the designer and the builder read CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped and TempTree's root seam (lesson #388).

components.name: Stopped-at-unlisted-peak memory Fact
components.responsibility:
AStoreStoppedAtItsUnlistedPeakFitsTheBudget runs in [Collection(nameof(MemoryBudget))], so it is serialised with FiveMillionEntriesFitTheMemoryBudget.
- It drives the store in scanner order: an explicit stack, one contiguous child block per listing, then SetChildren, then subfolders pushed last-first.
- The shape is U-001's and U-201's: 5,000,000 planned entries, 4.5M files and 0.5M folders, names of 5-48 characters, and 300,000 names sharing 100,000 IDs. A late folder W has 60,000 subfolders.
- It stops right after W's block is registered, at about 4.88M entries.

It asserts:
- NotListed count == the generator's own pending-stack count, and at least 60,000.
- GC-heap retained and sampled peak deltas under 800 MiB, measured exactly as ScanStoreBudgetTests does.
- Process private commit after Refresh() at the stop under 1 GiB. It records the commit before the build too, taken after a blocking, compacting, aggressive full collection.
- RolledSize(0) and FilesBelow(0) equal the generator's own totals.

Every figure goes to ITestOutputHelper.
components.key_interactions: FiveMillionEntriesFitTheMemoryBudget runs unedited. Its retained figure (654.6 MiB at the build-check baseline) is recorded at validate as the evidence that no per-entry storage was added. The WPF app's own commit at this shape is not measured here; it is filed for later.

components.name: Design record
components.responsibility:
Records:
- 'listed' means children registered by SetChildren, so NotListed, Unreadable and NotScanned are disjoint
- why bit 0x80 of Flags was chosen and why it is the last free bit
- the root boundary: stops in calls 1-2 leave no root
- that 'listed ahead but not yet written' is covered only by construction, and what a future read-ahead reader must keep
- the measured memory figures
- that Cancel on a stalled share is not re-measured by this slice (lesson #136)

Later slices, such as the 'not read yet' view U-182 asks for, find the contract here.
components.key_interactions: It is not a .taad record, so it edits no design-slice export (lesson #473), fitness.yaml, rules harness or WindowCases file (lesson #472).

key_decisions.decision: Store the mark as bit 0x80 of the existing per-entry Flags byte: not a new column, not a Kind bit, not a public EntryFlags member.
key_decisions.rationale: Criterion 7 forbids per-entry storage, and the build check measured 0x80 as free in Page.Flags. A Kind bit would break every Kind-branching read (survey warning; U-201's masking condition). The tag is 'expensive' because this spends the last free Flags bit (U-201 condition). The next flag needs a new byte column, about 4.8 MiB at 5M entries, or Kind's free bits with masking across seven reads.

key_decisions.decision: 'Listed' means 'children registered by SetChildren'. Unreadable folders and the NotScanned container store therefore read listed, and the three states never overlap.
key_decisions.rationale: Criteria 1 and 3 define the mark by registration, and FolderDone (Scanner.cs:377) and StoreSkipped (:336) do register those folders. Criterion 5 requires their classification to be exactly today's. The build check's warning about those two call sites is answered as intended behaviour. A later view maps each state to one phrase, so this meaning becomes a contract other slices build on.

key_decisions.decision: Hide the mark from Flags() and expose it only through the new public read ScanStore.NotListed(int).
key_decisions.rationale: Criterion 5. The spike's diagnostic measured that with the bit raw in Flags(), CancelledFolderTests.CancelAtAnyCallCommitsOnlyWholeFolders fails in both modes. Masked, every existing equality comparison and every src flag test (FolderTreeNode NotScanned, SizeProbe.IsEligible, Scanner.IsDue) sees today's values. D1 is the new read.

key_decisions.decision: Append and AddFlags throw ArgumentException on a caller-supplied 0x80, before any write, instead of silently stripping it the way Append strips HardlinkDuplicate.
key_decisions.rationale: Criterion 3 says every other path refuses the mark. No legitimate caller can name the bit, so an incoming 0x80 is always a defect and should fail loudly. Throwing before the count is published keeps the store unchanged. A repo-wide grep finds no `(EntryFlags)0x` anywhere in src or tests today, so no existing caller is affected.

key_decisions.decision: Append the root right after ListRoot's directory check, before DecideLastAccess, the keep reopen and the first List. A Stop in the root's open or attribute query (calls 1-2) still leaves Count 0.
key_decisions.rationale: This meets the risk spike's prerequisite (h): 20 of 20 root-listing Stops left no root. It also covers calls 3-5, which the spike reported still left none. The store state there (root appended, nothing listed) is the same state the spike's 'before List' variant validated at 964/964. The boundary has a reason: until the attribute query answers, nothing is known to be a folder. The fallback, if the build's sweep disagrees, is the spike's exact placement.

key_decisions.decision: Rely on construction for the 'listed ahead but not yet written' shape of criterion 1; build no read-ahead reader.
key_decisions.rationale: The build check measured a single-threaded depth-first walk with no read-ahead reader on any branch (lesson #144). The mark is cleared only by SetChildren, so a folder a future reader lists without registering stays NotListed. The case is on the matrix as material: false.

key_decisions.decision: Prove criteria 4 and 5 with the existing oracles. RollupOracle.Expected/AssertMatches runs over a Fed stream rebuilt from the stopped store's raw columns, which is the U-182-style recount independent of the store's posting and charge rule. CheckStructure runs too, and a masked twin replayed through RollupOracle.Feed.
key_decisions.rationale: The twin is literally 'the same store with the mark masked off', which is what criterion 5 asks for. No new oracle class or product seam is needed.

key_decisions.decision: Write two settled architecture rules: no src code outside the store casts 0x80/128 to EntryFlags, and EntryFlags names no member at 0x80. The proposal had declined any fitness rule.
key_decisions.rationale: Because Flags() masks the bit, a test of `Flags(e) & (EntryFlags)0x80` anywhere in src would compile, always be false, and silently read every unread folder as listed. The prose contract cannot catch that; a text rule does. Engine-appended settled rules have no xUnit twin. Because the settled count changes, validate runs `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-001` and `-Case C-003` once (lesson #212). Both globs match existing files, so the harness's unmatched-rule refusal (lesson #471) cannot fire.

key_decisions.decision: Measure criterion 7 with one new Core Fact in the MemoryBudget collection, stopped at the unlisted peak in U-201's shape. 'App commit' is recorded as the test host's private commit while it holds the stopped 5M store, and the WPF app's own figure is filed for later.
key_decisions.rationale: A Core Fact is the only unattended route to a 5M store in this tree's test style. A stopped ending never builds the tree (MainWindow.xaml.cs:606-607), so the WPF window adds roughly U-001's ~106 MB baseline. U-201 measured 808 MiB with the tree open, as an upper bound. Claiming the WPF figure as measured here would be false.

key_decisions.decision: Build only NotListed: no SubtreeUnfinished marker, no App view, no opt-in Trait.
key_decisions.rationale: The slice goal is unread versus empty. U-204 (both markers) is IMPOSSIBLE as stated. SubtreeUnfinished needs Kind masking and holds only under DFS (U-201), and a later slice can derive it from NotListed plus the walk order. The new 5M Fact runs in the default suite next to the existing one, so lesson #198's three-piece opt-in gating is not needed.

proposals.note: The only proposal. Taken whole, with its over_engineering_flag honoured: SubtreeUnfinished is dropped. Composer changes: two settled text rules added, which the proposal had declined; the container store pinned as m's only subfolder so the sweep oracle holds; criterion 6's 'no edits' made a git-diff check; and the WPF app's commit at this shape filed for later instead of claimed.

payload.coherence_check:
There was one proposal, so there was no composition to check, and nothing here has yet survived a disagreement. The reviewer is the first to argue with it.

The proposal's own pieces were checked against each other and against the tree for contradictory invariants:

(a) Mark clearing vs the disjoint states. SetChildren clears the mark, and FolderDone calls SetChildren before AddFlags(Unreadable) (Scanner.cs:377-383). StoreSkipped calls SetChildren before AddFlags(NotScanned) (:336-337). So NotListed, Unreadable and NotScanned are disjoint, consistent with the 'listed = registered' decision and with criterion 5.

(b) The masked Flags() vs IsDue/ProbeRule (:494-495) and every Assert.Equal(EntryFlags.X, Flags(e)). They see today's values, and a completed scan has no marks anyway.

(c) The early root append vs Execute's rootEntry < 0 branch. The out-parameter keeps its meaning, so Cancelled/RootUnreadable are decided as before. Scans.AssertChargedBytesAreTheTotals with Count 1 and an unseeded tracker is the state the spike's root-first variant ran at 964/964. Every test that pins Store.Count == 0 (RootTests:18, CancellationTests:58/:128, ContainerLayerStoreTests' Refused cases) stops at or before the directory check.

(d) Append's new refusal vs existing callers. No `(EntryFlags)0x` appears anywhere in src or tests. RollupOracle.Feed, ScanStoreBudgetTests and the AppendRoot callers pass named flags only.

(e) The masked twin vs CheckParent. CheckParent refuses appends under an Unreadable parent, so the twin is fed without Unreadable and has it added afterwards. Feed never calls SetChildren on a childless folder, so the twin explicitly registers those to clear its own marks.

(f) The sweep oracle vs StoreSkipped. StoreSkipped makes no guarded call and AfterFolder does not fire for it, so 'the store is committed iff m is' holds only if the store is m's only subfolder. The tree is specified that way. ContainerLayerStore.Resolve's guard is created with announce: false, so the Created hook never arms it.

(g) The new 5M Fact vs the existing one. Both run in the MemoryBudget collection, serialised. GC-heap deltas are per-test, but process private commit can still carry the earlier Fact's committed memory, which is recorded as a risk with an outside claim.

What was changed at the seams:
- Two architecture rules were added that the proposal had declined. Rule 1 exempts ScanStore.cs, the one file that may name the bit, and covers src only, because the new tests must cast 0x80 to prove the refusals.
- Criterion 7's 'app within 1 GiB' is stated as measured on the test host only, with the WPF residual filed for later.

The App is untouched by construction. A public read is added to ScanStore and Flags() semantics are unchanged for every named value. A consumer grep including tests/bugs/* (lesson #466) finds only named-flag reads, for example SL-063 DoneRowFinality's ProbeCorrected test.

No workaround for an outside defect is introduced. The existing wcifs-layer-store precaution's folder reads 'listed' (zero children registered) and keeps its NotScanned flag and notice, unchanged.

architecture_rules.name: no code outside the store spells the not-listed bit as an entry flag
architecture_rules.because: ScanStore.Flags() masks bit 0x80 off, and Append and AddFlags refuse it. Outside the store, `Flags(e) & (EntryFlags)0x80` compiles and is always false, so it silently reads every never-listed folder as listed. Passing the bit to a store write throws mid-scan. The one read of the mark is ScanStore.NotListed.

architecture_rules.name: EntryFlags names no member at the store's reserved bit
architecture_rules.because: Bit 0x80 of the flags byte is the not-listed mark. Flags() strips it from every read and Append and AddFlags refuse it on every write. A member named at that value would vanish from every read and throw on every write, and enumerating EntryFlags would start listing the mark, which criterion 5 forbids. The next flag needs a new byte column or Kind's free bits (U-201).

cases.behaviour: report which folders a stopped scan never listed
cases.shape: folders still queued on the stack when Stop lands between two folders, before or during any guarded call after their parent committed
cases.why: FolderDone pushes subfolders already appended with Append's defaults (FirstChild -1, ChildCount 0, rolled 0). The build check measured these as identical to a listed-empty folder in every read. Only the mark tells them apart.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.NotListedTests.CancelAtAnyCallMarksExactlyTheFoldersNotCommitted" (both InlineData: before and during)

cases.behaviour: report which folders a stopped scan never listed
cases.shape: the folder is cut part-way through a listing that spans several 64 KiB buffers ('big': 2,000 names of 100 characters), with Stop between two buffers or during one
cases.why: DirectoryReader.List zeroes its count on an abort, and FolderDone returns at Cancelled before AddEntry and SetChildren (Scanner.cs:370-371). Any partial-commit path, or a SetChildren reached on the cut folder, would clear the mark on a folder whose children were never registered. The sweep asserts bigBuffers > 1, so the between-buffers case is really exercised.
cases.check: NotListedTests.CancelAtAnyCallMarksExactlyTheFoldersNotCommitted, at every k inside big's calls, in both modes (same command as above)

cases.behaviour: report the root as never listed
cases.shape: Stop lands inside the root's own handling after its directory check: the last-access queries, the keep reopen, or any listing call of a 2,000-entry root, before and during
cases.why: Risk spike (h): ListRoot appended the root only after List, so 20 of 20 such Stops left an empty store with nothing to mark. Calls 3-5 also still left no root in the spike's variant. The early append must leave Count 1, NotListed(0), ChildCount(0) 0, status Cancelled and RootError 0.

cases.behaviour: report the root as never listed
cases.shape: Stop lands in the root's open or attribute query (calls 1-2), the token is cancelled before the scan starts, or the picked root is a file
cases.why: This is the boundary of the early append. Until the attribute query answers, nothing is known to be a folder, so these must still leave Count 0 with status Cancelled, or RootUnreadable 267 for a file, exactly as the existing tests pin.
cases.check: NotListedTests.AStopInTheRootsListingLeavesTheRootNotListed asserts Count 0 for k ≤ 2. The existing RootTests.ARegularFileIsNotARoot, CancellationTests.CancelReturnsFromAScanStuckInItsFirstCall and CancellationTests.AnAlreadyCancelledTokenReadsNothing also pass unedited (--filter "FullyQualifiedName~RootTests|FullyQualifiedName~CancellationTests").

cases.behaviour: tell a listed empty folder from an unread one
cases.shape: an empty folder listed before the Stop, with unlisted folders queued behind it: a-empty, b\c\f.bin and z\g.bin, stopped through AfterFolder after 2 and after 3 folders, and the same tree completed
cases.why: SetChildren(folder, first, 0) writes the same FirstChild -1 and ChildCount 0 that Append wrote (ScanStore.cs:257-258). The mark's clearing for a count of 0 is the only thing that separates a-empty from b, z and b\c.

cases.behaviour: report which folders a stopped scan never listed
cases.shape: Stop lands during the size probes, after every folder's listing committed
cases.why: The status is Cancelled, but every folder's children were registered. A mark tied to status or to the probe pass, or a reader assuming 'Cancelled means not listed', would wrongly report folders as unread.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.NotListedTests.AStopDuringSizingLeavesEveryFolderListed" (the ScanOptions.Probe seam cancels on its first probe)

cases.behaviour: keep the mark's writes to the two store calls
cases.shape: a caller passes bit 0x80 to Append (folder, file and link, alone and with each named flag) or to AddFlags (on a marked folder and on a listed one)
cases.why: Measured today: Append stores 0x80 and AddFlags ORs it in, and the only guard is HardlinkDuplicate's. The refusal must throw before any column or the count is written, so Count and the target's flags are unchanged afterwards.

cases.shape: the folder is still marked while its children are appended under it, as FolderDone does before SetChildren, and SetChildren then registers 0 or n of them
cases.why: CheckParent runs on every child append before SetChildren (Scanner.cs:375-377). A parent check that read the mark would refuse every listing. SetChildren's count-0 branch (FirstChild -1) must clear the mark too.

cases.behaviour: keep the mark's writes to the two store calls
cases.shape: an entry receives every other flag write: AddFlags of each named flag on a marked and a listed folder, CorrectSizes under a chain of marked folders, and file and link appends
cases.why: AddFlags ORs into the same byte, and Append ORs HardlinkDuplicate in after TryAddFileId. A mask slip in either would set the bit on a file or clear it on a folder. Criterion 3 says only append sets it and only SetChildren clears it.

cases.behaviour: read store figures over a stopped store
cases.shape: stores stopped at several points of the sweep tree: inside big, between h1 and h2, inside the root's listing, and just after m
cases.why: RolledSize, OnDiskAtOrBelow, FilesBelow, ChildrenLargestFirst and CheckParent branch on the Kind byte, and Charges on Kind plus HardlinkDuplicate. A mark that leaked into Kind or Charges would zero folders or double-count hardlinks with nothing failing (lesson #68). The recount reads raw columns and its own first-seen ID set, independent of the store's posting.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.NotListedTests.AStoppedStoreRecountsWithNoDifference". It runs RollupOracle.Expected/AssertMatches plus CheckStructure plus a ChildrenLargestFirst sort check, and requires 0 differences.

cases.behaviour: classify unreadable, left-out and hardlink-charged entries in a stopped store
cases.shape: a stopped store holding a denied folder (Unreadable), the planted container layer store (NotScanned), unlisted folders and an h1/h2 hardlink pair, compared with its replayed twin that carries no marks
cases.why: FolderDone and StoreSkipped call SetChildren before AddFlags, so those folders read listed, and their flags must be exactly today's. Record-equality comparisons (Scans.EntryState) and enumeration must never see the bit: the spike measured 2 failures when it showed raw.
cases.check: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.NotListedTests.AStoppedStoreClassifiesAsItsMaskedTwin|FullyQualifiedName~FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.CancelledFolderTests.CancelAtAnyCallCommitsOnlyWholeFolders". The first also asserts that Enum.GetValues<EntryFlags>() has no member carrying 0x80 and that Flags() never returns it.

cases.shape: a completed scan of the sweep tree, and of a tree holding a junction and a path over 260 characters
cases.why: Every folder of a completed walk must have reached SetChildren. Links are recorded and never entered, so they must never be marked. With all marks clear, a completed scan's flags are exactly today's, and the existing store, counting-rule and last-access tests must pass unedited.
cases.check: NotListedTests.ACompletedScanLeavesNothingNotListed. Then `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx` green, with at least the 964 baseline tests plus the new ones, 0 failed. `git diff --diff-filter=M --name-only 6ce263e -- tests` must print nothing.

cases.shape: a 5M-entry store driven in scanner order and stopped at its unlisted peak: the late folder W's 60,000 subfolders registered, about 4.88M entries, and at least 60,000 folders marked
cases.why: Criterion 7. The existing budget test covers only a completed-shape store and records no process commit. The unlisted peak is where U-201 measured the store 97.6% full, the worst case.

contracts.name: ScanStore.NotListed(int index) : bool
contracts.auth_model: public read, same as the other ScanStore reads
contracts.error_cases: ArgumentOutOfRangeException for an index outside [0, Count), through At.
contracts.notes:
True only for a folder that was appended and whose children were never registered:
- still queued when the scan stopped
- cut by Stop part-way through its listing, which commits nothing
- the root, when the scan stopped or the root's listing failed with nothing kept, after the directory check and before the listing committed
- by construction, a folder a future reader listed ahead without writing

False for:
- a folder whose listing committed, empty or not, including a folder flagged Unreadable and the NotScanned container store, so the three states never overlap
- every file and link
- every entry once a scan completes

Exact between appends on the writing thread and after Scan returns. A read from another thread during a scan is outside the contract, as for the rollups (U-170, U-172).

contracts.name: ScanStore.Flags(int index) never includes bit 0x80
contracts.notes: Returns the stored byte with 0x80 masked off, so every existing equality comparison and flag test sees exactly today's values. EntryFlags gains no member.

contracts.name: ScanStore.Append / AppendRoot set the mark on folders and refuse it from callers
contracts.error_cases: ArgumentException when the flags passed carry 0x80, thrown before any column or the count is written. All existing exceptions stay as they are.
contracts.notes: kind == Folder sets the bit before the count is published; File and Link never do. HardlinkDuplicate is still silently cleared, as today.

contracts.name: ScanStore.AddFlags refuses the mark
contracts.error_cases: ArgumentException when the flags carry 0x80, as for HardlinkDuplicate; the entry is unchanged.
contracts.notes: AddFlags only ORs, so it can never clear the mark. No flag-clearing path exists or is added.

contracts.name: ScanStore.SetChildren clears the mark
contracts.notes: The only write that clears the mark, for any count including 0. Order: FirstChild, ChildCount, then the flag byte. The only Scanner callers stay FolderDone and StoreSkipped.

contracts.name: Scanner.Scan result shape when the root fails or is stopped
contracts.error_cases: Once the root has passed the directory check, a Cancelled result, or a RootUnreadable result whose listing failed with nothing kept, holds exactly one entry: the root, reading NotListed with ChildCount 0. Status, RootError, Totals, Unreadable and FileIdsAvailable are as today. A root refused at its open or attribute query, a non-directory root, an already-cancelled token and a Refused root still leave Count 0.
contracts.notes: The App returns early on RootUnreadable and builds the tree only for Completed scans (ShowOutcome). LargestFiles and KindBreakdown over a root-only store yield nothing, as they do for an empty root folder today.

code_claims.claim: Append starts every entry with FirstChild -1 and ChildCount 0. It stores the flags it is given with only HardlinkDuplicate masked off, and it writes the flags byte before Volatile.Write publishes the new count.
SetChildren writes FirstChild (-1 when the count is 0) and ChildCount, and writes no flags.
AddFlags throws ArgumentException only when HardlinkDuplicate is passed, and otherwise ORs whatever bits it is given into the flags byte.
CheckParent refuses a parent that is not a Folder by its Kind byte, or that carries the Unreadable bit, and tests no other flag bit.
Charges is true only for Kind File with the HardlinkDuplicate bit clear, so a bit-0x80 mark on a folder cannot change any charge.
The public Flags(index) read today returns the raw flags byte cast to EntryFlags, so any bit stored there would show through.
AppendRoot throws unless the store is empty, and appends the root as a Folder with EntryFlags.None through Append.
Each page has a byte[] Flags column of PageSize entries next to a separate byte[] Kind column, so an unused Flags bit costs no added storage.
EntryFlags is a byte [Flags] enum whose named values use bits 1 through 64 (Unreadable through NotScanned), which leaves 0x80 unnamed.
RolledSize returns the RolledSize column when the Kind byte is Folder, and otherwise branches on Charges; it reads no flag beyond HardlinkDuplicate.
FilesBelow switches on the Kind byte alone: Folder gives the FilesBelow column, File gives 1, anything else gives 0.
ChildrenLargestFirst returns an empty array when the Kind byte is not Folder or ChildCount is 0; otherwise it ranks each child by OnDiskAtOrBelow.
OnDiskAtOrBelow branches on the Kind byte for folders and on Charges for files.

FolderDone returns true before any append when ClassifyReadError gives Cancelled. Otherwise it appends every listed entry, calls SetChildren(folder, first, count), and only then adds Unreadable when FailedKind is non-null.
StoreSkipped calls SetChildren(folder, Count, 0), then AddFlags NotScanned, records the folder in _skipped, and makes no guarded call.

ListRoot opens the root, queries its attributes, refuses a non-directory with ERROR_DIRECTORY, decides last-access handling and may reopen. It appends the root through AppendRoot only after _reader.List has succeeded or kept entries.

When ListRoot returns rootEntry < 0, Execute ends Cancelled or RootUnreadable. Otherwise it commits the root through FolderDone, then pops _pending, sending each folder to StoreSkipped or to _reader.Read followed by FolderDone.
IsDue passes the public _store.Flags(entry) read to the probe rule.
Resolve's store decision opens through a SynchronousIoCancel created with announce: false, before the scan's own guard exists.
ShowOutcome returns early on RootUnreadable, and calls ShowFolderTree only when the status is Completed; a stopped scan keeps its list.
EntryState is a record of Kind, Flags, Attributes, Size, OnDisk, FileId and ChildCount, and Snapshot fills it from the public Flags() read, so stopped stores are compared on flag equality.
AssertChargedBytesAreTheTotals returns early for an empty store. Otherwise it runs RollupOracle.CheckStructure and compares the root's Rolled.Of with the scan's Totals.
RunCancellingAt runs a scan with Cancel fed in at the scan thread's k-th guarded call, either before the call or during it.
The test sweeps every guarded call and expects each folder not committed to equal the uncancelled baseline's state with ChildCount 0 and SizeProbed masked, compared by EntryState record equality.
Expected recomputes every entry's totals from a Fed stream with its own first-seen ID set and its own rule for what charges, and reads nothing from the store.

Feed builds a store through AppendRoot and Append only, and after each non-root append calls SetChildren on that entry's parent, so a folder that never receives a child is never passed to SetChildren.
MemoryBudget is a collection with DisableParallelization. ScanStoreBudgetTests runs in it and asserts a completed-shape 5M-entry store stays under StoreBudget, 800 MiB, measured as GC-heap deltas.
The test asserts that a file picked as the root ends RootUnreadable with error 267 and Store.Count 0.
The test asserts Store.Count 0 when Cancel interrupts the scan's first guarded call, the root's open.

code_claims.symbol: probe results are applied only on the listing thread

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: database storage engines: row commit status (a tuple is written marked in-progress, only the commit step resolves it, and an aborted writer leaves rows that read as uncommitted rather than absent or empty)
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: Mark at creation, clear only at the one commit step, and make the mark readable after the writer stops. A stopped writer then leaves 'never committed' as a positive fact, instead of something inferred from default values that look the same as 'committed empty'.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: Selected in full. Append's defaults look exactly like a folder committed empty (measured by the build check). The fix has the commit bit's shape: written before the entry is published, cleared only by the single registering call. It transfers because the store has one writer and one commit call per folder.

invariants.precondition: There is a single writer, and a folder's commit is one call
invariants.evidence: Scanner remarks: depth-first on the caller's thread, and ThreadOwner guards Credit and Correct. SetChildren is called only at Scanner.cs:377 (FolderDone) and :336 (StoreSkipped).

invariants.precondition: The mark is written before the entry becomes visible
Every folder that reaches commit goes through that one call
invariants.evidence: FolderDone's non-cancel path always calls SetChildren, Unreadable folders included. StoreSkipped calls it for the NotScanned store. The root goes through FolderDone.

invariants.precondition: No other path sets or clears the mark
invariants.evidence: Today Append stores 0x80 and AddFlags accepts it (measured). The slice adds the refusals, and the cases 'a caller passes bit 0x80' and 'every other flag write' check them. Architecture rule 1 fences src code outside the store.

invariants.precondition: A creation point exists for every folder the scan knows about, the root included
invariants.evidence: Risk spike (h): a Stop in the root's listing left no root entry, 20 of 20. Fixed here by appending right after the directory check. The spike's 'before List' variant left 20/20 roots NotListed at 964/964. Stops in calls 1-2 still leave no root, by design.
The store is frozen once Scan returns (lesson #144). Live cross-thread reads are excluded by the ScanStore remarks, and U-170 and U-172 are IMPOSSIBLE and out of scope.

channeled_experts: storage-engine commit-status design (a record is born in-progress, only commit clears it)
disk-usage tool maintainers (ncdu / WinDirStat per-directory state flags)

prior_art.pattern: A finished or empty result is believed even though no work happened. Tell 'the request completed' apart from 'the work was done': the same failure as a stopped store whose unread folders look empty.
Keep folder state as an explicit enumerated state (idle, scanning, scan-waiting, ...) rather than inferring it from contents.
Disk-usage browsers carry distinct per-directory marks for a read error, an error below, excluded, and an empty directory, so 'empty' is never inferred from a zero size.
Each tree item tracks whether its own read is done, so partially read subtrees are distinguishable while and after reading.
A row is written carrying an in-progress transaction marker that only commit resolves; after an abort it reads as uncommitted rather than vanishing or looking valid.
prior_art.where: PostgreSQL MVCC tuple header (xmin with commit-status lookup)

outside_claims.claim: When Stop lands while the scanner is blocked in a directory query on a stalled SMB session, the cut folder's Read returns 995 with LastCallAborted true. ClassifyReadError then gives Cancelled, so SetChildren is never called and the folder keeps its mark.
outside_claims.source: risk spike smb-stalled-listing-stop-keeps-cut-folder-unlisted: 20/20, Windows Sandbox build 26100, SMBLibrary rig; Windows 10 and other builds not measured
outside_claims.if_wrong: A share folder cut by Stop would be recorded Unreadable with its kept entries, and would read listed although its listing never finished.

outside_claims.claim: A 2,000-entry folder with 100-character names spans more than one 64 KiB listing buffer on local NTFS, so a Stop can land between two buffers of one folder.
outside_claims.source: CancelledFolderTests asserts bigBuffers > 1 and passed in the build check's 964/964 baseline
outside_claims.if_wrong: The 'cut part-way between buffers' shape would not be exercised; the sweep's own assertion would fail and say so.

outside_claims.claim: A deny ACE set through TempTree.Deny makes the folder's open or listing fail for the current user with Win32 error 5, so the scan records it Unreadable.
outside_claims.source: U-180 and U-189 fixtures (ACL-denied folders, win32 5 NothingListed) and the existing Unreadable-folder counting-rule tests
outside_claims.if_wrong: The masked-twin case would carry no Unreadable folder and could not show that its classification is unchanged.

outside_claims.claim: Enum.GetValues<TEnum>() returns only the enum's named members, so an unnamed bit 0x80 can never appear in an enumeration of EntryFlags.
outside_claims.if_wrong: Criterion 5's 'code that lists every flag ignores the mark' would need an explicit filter in consumers; no product code enumerates EntryFlags today.

outside_claims.claim: A blocking, compacting GC.Collect with GCCollectionMode.Aggressive returns freed GC memory to the OS. Process.PrivateMemorySize64 after Refresh() then reports the process's current private commit, without most of what an earlier 5M-entry Fact in the same test host committed.
outside_claims.if_wrong: The new Fact's absolute 'private commit under 1 GiB' figure could include the earlier Fact's leftovers and fail or mislead. The GC-heap deltas against the 800 MiB store bound are unaffected, and the build reports the before-build commit next to the at-stop one.

taste_disagreements: Rules or none: the proposal declined any fitness rule, to stay out of rules-harness and RuleCases cost (lessons #472, #212). The composer added two settled text rules, because the bit-test-outside-the-store defect is silent. Reverting them costs nothing but the guard.

Refuse vs strip: Append could strip a caller's 0x80 silently, as it does HardlinkDuplicate, instead of throwing. The design throws because criterion 3 says the other paths 'refuse' it. Either choice is a one-line change.

Root boundary: 'append after the directory check', which covers calls 3-5, vs the spike's validated 'append before the first List call'. The design takes the earlier point. The sweep test settles whether it holds.

Naming: NotListed(int) reports the negative state, where IsListed(int) would report the positive. The negative was chosen so the default for a never-touched folder reads true. Nobody else has weighed in.

whats_new: ScanStore: private NotListedBit (0x80). Append sets it on folders and refuses it from callers, SetChildren clears it, AddFlags refuses it, and Flags() masks it.
ScanStore.NotListed(int): a public read reporting a folder whose children were never registered (D1).
EntryKind.cs: a comment reserving bit 0x80 for the store, outside the EntryFlags enum.

Scanner.ListRoot: the root is appended right after the directory check, before the last-access decision, the keep reopen and the listing, so a Stop in any of those leaves a root reading NotListed (spike prerequisite (h)).
Scanner remarks: folders cut part-way or never reached now read NotListed.
